surrounding_order.text: D-value is defined as the time required at a given temperature to reduce the microbial population by 90% (one log₁₀ reduction).
It is widely used to measure the effectiveness of sterilization and disinfection processes.
Example:If D₁₂₁ = 2 minutes, it means 90% of organisms are killed in 2 minutes at 121°C.

cells.text: Time to kill 90% at a given temperature

surrounding_order.text: Modified Faine’s criteria is a diagnostic scoring system for leptospirosis.
Clinical features (fever, headache, myalgia, conjunctival suffusion, jaundice, etc.)
Epidemiological factors (exposure to contaminated water, rodents, occupation)
A total score ≥ a defined cutoff supports the diagnosis of leptospirosis, especially in endemic areas.
Rheumatic fever → diagnosed using Jones criteria
Bacterial vaginosis → diagnosed using Amsel’s criteria/Nugent score
Systemic lupus erythematosus → diagnosed using ACR/EULAR criteria

surrounding_order.text: Correct Ans: B) Target modification from D-Ala-D-Ala to D-Ala-D-Lac
Vancomycin inhibits cell wall synthesis by binding to the D-Ala-D-Ala terminus of the peptidoglycan precursors.
Enterococci develop resistance by altering the target site, so vancomycin cannot bind.
Key genes: vanA, vanB, vanC, vanD, vanE, vanG
Most clinically significant: vanA and vanB

cells.text: Changes peptidoglycan terminus from D-Ala-D-Ala → D-Ala-D-Lac → ↓ binding affinity
Variable resistance to vancomycin, susceptible to teicoplanin
Intrinsic, low-level resistance in E. gallinarum/E. casseliflavus
